data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds array read from unchecked table index)
data.rationale: VERIFIED empirically: a standalone ASAN build of flb_hash.c reports 'heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 ... flb_hash_get_by_id src/flb_hash.c:375' when id (200) >= ht->size (1). flb_hash_get_by_id() dereferences ht->table[id] (flb_hash.c:374) without validating that id is within ht->size, the number of flb_hash_table slots allocated by flb_hash_create(). Every other accessor in flb_hash.c derives its index via (hash %% ht->size), so this is the only unchecked path. Reachability: the OSS-Fuzz harness tests/internal/fuzzers/utils_fuzzer.c calls flb_hash_create((int)(data[2] %% 0x04), (size_t)data[0], (int)data[1]) and then loops flb_hash_get_by_id(ht, (int)data[i], ...) for i in 0..19. data[i] is a raw fuzz byte (0..255) while ht->size is data[0] (can be as small as 1), so any input where data[0] < some data[i] (i<20) makes table point up to 255*sizeof(struct flb_hash_table) bytes past the end of the heap allocation. The subsequent read of table->count (flb_hash.c:375) is an ASAN heap-buffer-overflow READ. Any fuzz corpus with size >= 600 and a small data[0] triggers it; the fix is bounds-checking id against ht->size before the dereference.
